title.title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
title.subtitle: Claim: two closed aspherical 4-manifolds are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic

plain: Two four-dimensional spaces that match in every loose, stretchy sense, but can't be matched point for point

object.heading: Two-colour a cycle: even length works, odd length cannot

beats.text: The combinatorial core, schematically: 2-colour a cycle red and blue
An odd cycle always leaves two neighbours with the same colour
Marked fillings exist only for even $d$, so the two manifolds cannot be homeomorphic

steps: A homeomorphism would give a marked filling for an odd cover
Fillings colour plumbing caps red and blue, in alternation
An odd cycle can't be coloured that way: no homeomorphism

achievement.label: Borel conjecture (1953), dimension 4
achievement.context: Before: true in dimension at most 3, and for hyperbolic groups in dimension 5 and up (Bartels–Lück 2012)
achievement.note: Imports the invariant of family 305 as a black box; only as solid as 305

verify.detail: Manuscript only: 60 pages; the odd-cycle colouring core is checkable
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Colour a cycle red and blue, neighbours different. An odd cycle always clashes.
A homeomorphism would force a clean colouring of an odd cycle. Impossible.
Claimed: same homotopy type, yet not homeomorphic.

sources.quote: Borel (1953 letter to Serre). True in dims <= 3 (geometrization), and for large classes of groups in dims >= 5 (Farrell-Jones; Bartels-Lueck 2012 for hyperbolic and CAT(0) groups).
There exist closed connected aspherical topological 4-manifolds M, N with common word-hyperbolic fundamental group that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic
so it is only as solid as 305. The combinatorial core (odd-cycle colouring argument) is checkable. 60 pages.

sources.ref: article, Disc embedding, Wall's PD4 question and the Borel conjecture
sources.quote: a chamber whose $d$-fold cyclic covers have marked fillings exactly when $d$ is even, decided by trying to 2-colour an odd cycle.
